title: Strategy Ladder UI for batching + cache heuristics
creator: Priya Menon
description: Design a compact, progressive UI pattern (the 'Strategy Ladder') that helps operators choose batching + prefix/KV caching configurations. The UI should explain tradeoffs (latency vs. unit cost vs. quality risk), surface recommended presets, and include lightweight simulations and guardrails for safe rollouts. Aim is to reduce trial-and-error during adoption and lower support overhead for new Dedicated and Private customers.
design_notes: Goal: combine recommendations, a concise explainer, and a one-click simulation to preview token cost and latency impact.
Psych: users respond better to ranked options with clear dominant 'safest' choice plus 2 progressive alternatives (balanced, aggressive).
Key components: ladder of presets, micro-simulate panel (sample traffic), risk band indicator, inline rollback toggle, and contextual help links.
Constraints: small vertical real estate in the model-config flow; must be readable at width 540px for side rail and 980px for full page.
Accessibility: ensure color-contrast for risk bands and provide textual equivalents for protector rules.
Localization: strings should be short to support 10+ locales in the console.
Interoperability: presets map to runtime profiles (quantization, kernel hints, batching window ms, prefix_cache TTL), must serialize to runtime-1.18 rollout API fields.
Telemetry hooks: every preset selection fires event with prior/after profile ids to power Optimize suggestions.
Security: no customer prompt content is transmitted to design prototypes; sample traffic is synthetic.
Edge-case: when a model has stateful chat with large prefix sizes, warn and disable 'aggressive' presets.
Success metrics: reduction in support tickets about 'incorrect batching' and 20% adoption of recommended presets in first 30 days.
review_feedback: PM (Miguel Soto): prefer a clearer primary action copy than 'Apply' — suggested 'Enable preset & simulate'.
Eng (Connor Hayes): needs deterministic mapping to runtime configs; asked for table of fields to map (batch_window_ms, max_batch_tokens, prefix_cache_mode, kv_cache_ttl).
Security (Aisha Raman): ensure prototype doesn't preload any real customer prefixes; flagged telemetry PII check.
Research (Zoe Kim): split A/B to test ladder vs single-recommendation; suggested two-week pilot for new customers.
Design critique: ladder labels should avoid value-laden words like 'cheap' or 'unsafe' — use 'Cost-lean', 'Balanced', 'Latency-first'.
tasks: Finalize ladder copy and microcopy; incorporate PM and security feedback.
Create mapping doc (design -> runtime fields) and hand off to ENG.
Prototype micro-simulate panel with three synthetic workloads (interactive chat, async embedding, reranker).
Implement risk-band visuals and alt text for accessibility.
Prepare A/B pilot plan and metrics dashboard (console + analytics).
Add E2E acceptance tests for preset serialization and rollback path.
Schedule design review with runtime and product (target 2026-03-18).
acceptance_criteria: Design spec includes ladder component with three presets and contextual explainers for each preset.
Prototype simulates expected latency and token-cost deltas for three sample workloads and allows toggling sample size.
Mapping doc lists exact runtime fields and default values for each preset and is approved by ENG.
Risk band displays color + textual interpretation and is accessible via keyboard and screen reader.
UX copy approved by PM and legal; no PII appears in prototype telemetry.
Pilot plan includes success metrics and rollout gate for disabling aggressive presets on stateful chats.
Design handoff artifacts (figma frames, spec spreadsheet, strings file) uploaded to Confluence and linked from ticket.
Prototype passed cross-team design review with actionable comments closed.
Release notes draft for console-2026.04 describing new UI and recommended rollout guidance.
